title: A Session that stops short is Nudged by the driver

statements.says: A step whose Session ends with work still owed is resumed by the driver with a Nudge, at most twice, before the loop stops.
A failed check that proves the work was done earns a Nudge: a review's heading, a build that changed the tree, or a finish that committed, left the tree Clean and closed the ticket.
A failed check that proves the Session could run earns no Nudge.
The Nudge names each check that failed.
The Nudge says that any command the Session left in the background was stopped with its last turn.
The Nudge asks the Session to say what blocks it if something does.
Every Session runs with a Bash limit of 45 minutes, by default and at most, so a long command finishes in the foreground.
The log says when a step was Nudged and so took longer.
The architecture review runs only the commands the placement-checks file names, not the Suite.
Carrying on cannot mend a Session that errored, loaded no command, or found its ticket closed.
An architecture review ran the script tests with a ten-minute limit, they took 17 and a half minutes, and Claude Code moved the command to the background.
Under claude -p nothing notifies a Session when a background command ends, because the process kills its background shells about five seconds after the last result.
The Session said it would wait, ended its turn and never wrote its report, so the heading check stopped the loop and a finished build and two passed reviews went to a Kept branch.
An earlier run hit the same limit and passed only because that Session read the output file instead of waiting.

Anthropic's guidance for unattended runs says an agent can end its turn with a report while work is still owed, so a harness treats that end as a report, names what is still open, and stops after two or three continuations.
The raised Bash limit removes the cause, and the Nudge catches a Session that backgrounds something and stops anyway.
The driver runs the whole Suite as its own step, so the architecture review was running tests it never read.
A Stop hook in each Session was rejected, because it moves a gate back inside the Session and the driver keeps its own check beside it, so one fact is checked twice.
A Stop hook was also rejected because it only runs inside a real Session, so no deterministic test can prove it.
A Stop hook was also rejected because a blocked stop brings back no output from a background command, and Claude Code ends the turn after eight blocks, which a long Suite can use up.
A Stop hook would earn its place if background shells came back despite the raised limit, because it is the one option that acts before claude -p kills them.

Turning off background tasks with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS was rejected, because it is a switch Claude Code offers rather than something Anthropic advises, and it takes away running two long checks at once.
Nudging only a review that wrote no heading was rejected, because a build is the most expensive step to lose and it can stop short the same way.
